Re: Internal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Cameron Foster  
Member ID: W291434326  
Plan: Aetna Commercial/ACA — Nevada  
Requested service: Primary total hip arthroplasty  
CPT: 27130  
Reference number: POC-503C0E1587-87184  
Date of denial: August 20, 2026

Dear Aetna Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document extensive conservative treatment, as well as the clinical findings supporting medical necessity.

Aetna’s publicly available Hip Arthroplasty Clinical Policy Bulletin, policy number 0287, states that total hip arthroplasty is medically necessary when there is advanced joint disease and a history of unsuccessful conservative therapy. The policy requires a history of unsuccessful conservative therapy that is clearly addressed in the medical record, with at least half of the required treatment consisting of formal, in-person physical therapy during the past year.

The records satisfy those requirements:

- I completed 14 weeks of supervised, in-person physical therapy from March 24, 2026, through June 30, 2026.
- I completed 24 physical therapy visits focused on hip-abductor strengthening and gait.
- The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of this treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026. It provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- My hip pain has progressively worsened for 18 months and has not been relieved by rest.

The policy also states that the conservative treatment for osteoarthritis, traumatic arthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or avascular necrosis should include anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics, flexibility and muscle-strengthening exercises, activity modification, and supervised physical therapy. My records document the medication trial and supervised physical therapy, including strengthening and gait treatment. The limited benefit from medication and injection, together with persistent symptoms despite physical therapy, demonstrates failure of conservative management rather than an absence of conservative treatment.

The records also document advanced clinical and functional impairment:

- A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated June 13, 2026, shows superolateral joint-space narrowing to 1 mm, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes.
- Hip range of motion is limited by pain.
- Provocative testing is positive on the affected side.
- I require a cane for ambulation.
- I can walk only one block.
- I cannot put on my shoes without assistance.
- Symptoms have persisted and progressed for 18 months.

Aetna’s policy identifies pain and functional disability interfering with activities of daily living, limited range of motion, and radiographic evidence of moderate or severe hip joint disease as relevant medical-necessity criteria. The records address each of those areas through the documented pain-related motion loss, severe functional limitations, and radiographic abnormalities.

The records also document factors relevant to surgical risk assessment: BMI 29, no smoking, no active infection, and no untreated substance use. The treating orthopedic surgeon is Reyes, MD.

For these reasons, I request that Aetna overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27130. Please have the orthopedic clinical reviewer consider the attached physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, imaging report, examination findings, and functional limitations.

If Aetna continues to deny authorization, please provide the specific clinical-review criteria and policy version used for this determination, including the effective or revision date, and identify precisely which criterion Aetna considers unsatisfied. The publicly available policy page does not display an effective or last-revised date, so please provide the version that was in effect when this request was reviewed.

Please also provide written confirmation that this appeal was received and the expected decision date. This appeal is submitted before the February 16, 2027 deadline stated in the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Cameron Foster  
[Mailing address]

[Email address]
